title: [Bounty $2,000] Restore OpenVLA execution and action correctness
author: jberkowitzTT
body:
# 📝 Background

OpenVLA (openvla/openvla-7b) in models/experimental/openvla has reported runtime failures on a single Wormhole N150 and produces robot actions that do not align with the Hugging Face reference. The report attributes the output errors to three issues: missing SigLIP positional embeddings, missing Q/K weight permutation, and an off-by-one error when assembling the action-token sequence.

The submitted fixes were tested on N150. This bounty is for a working, tested OpenVLA path—not a performance optimization or a real-robot benchmark.

# 🎯 What Success Looks Like

Submit one PR that satisfies all criteria below:
- OpenVLA initializes and runs end-to-end inference on a single Wormhole N150 using the repository’s supported environment, without manual runtime patches.
- SigLIP patch embeddings include the checkpoint’s positional embeddings, and a deterministic regression test compares the resulting features with the Hugging Face reference.
- Q/K weights are mapped into the layout expected by the OpenVLA attention/RoPE path. A regression test compares intermediate language-model outputs with the Hugging Face reference.
- predict_action returns the action tokens in the correct sequence, including the first action token produced during prefill; it does not shift action dimensions or use the EOS token as an action dimension.
- Automated regression coverage checks SigLIP features, early-layer logits or hidden states, and decoded actions against a fixed reference checkpoint and fixed inputs. Document the reference environment and the numerical tolerances; agree those tolerances with the OpenVLA owner before final review. Include at least one stable case that checks token ordering explicitly.
- The N150 end-to-end test and relevant existing OpenVLA tests pass. Provide the exact commands and test results in the PR.
- No unrelated model behavior or test failures are introduced. Performance optimization, N300/T3K/Blackhole validation, and a LIBERO/Bridge or other robot benchmark are out of scope.

# 💡 Problem to Solve

The report identifies three correctness defects:

- The SigLIP path applies patch embeddings without adding the checkpoint’s pos_embed before the encoder.
- OpenVLA’s Hugging Face-to-Meta key mapping renames weights but does not apply the Q/K permutation used by the TT-Transformers loader for the configured RoPE layout.
- The action decoder keeps the prefill-produced first action token separately, then returns later decode tokens as the action sequence, shifting the action dimensions and allowing EOS to be interpreted as the gripper action.
- It also reports seven N150 runtime blockers on the reported baseline (07fac6de536):
- Transformers accesses language_model before initialization in _supports_sdpa.
- post_init calls tie_weights with an unsupported argument.
- generate passes a cache object that fails an assertion.
- OpenVLA passes the string "prefill" where the TT-Transformers API expects Mode.PREFILL.
- Prefill RoPE uses the row-major cosine matrix instead of the prefill-specific slice.
- The timm version check rejects a version allowed by the declared dependency range.
- The test requests FABRIC_1D on a one-chip mesh, which is rejected by current fabric initialization.
- Before opening the bounty, confirm which reported runtime failures still reproduce on current main; remove any already-resolved items from the final scope. The reported pre-existing test_siglip_intermediate failure is not part of this bounty unless the owner confirms it is required to validate these fixes.


Original model integration: [PR #34985](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/pull/34985).

title: [Bounty $750] Fix remaining sharded scale_mask_softmax mask handling issues
author: jberkowitzTT
body:
📝 Background

ttnn.scale_mask_softmax_in_place with SoftmaxShardedMultiCoreProgramConfig can hang or read incorrect mask values when the input shard layout and mask shape/specification do not align. These cases can break correctness in sharded attention workloads and may hang the device instead of returning a clear validation error.

An open change already addresses the causal-mask case where a shard is shorter than or not divisible by the mask height, and the causal mask/input batch-size mismatch. This bounty is for the remaining issues below; coordinate with that change and do not duplicate its scope: [PR #63692](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/pull/63692).

🎯 What Success Looks Like

A row-major mask combined with is_causal_mask=True is either handled correctly or rejected during validation with a clear error before device execution; it must not hang.

Causal interleaved mask readers wrap rows using the mask’s height, not the input width. Non-square causal masks produce correct results without out-of-bounds reads.

Mask addressing remains correct when a shard crosses a batch boundary; the batch cursor must not advance early or read beyond the mask tensor.

A sharded mask with an incompatible shard specification (including shard orientation) is rejected clearly or handled correctly; it must not silently read a different core’s shard.

Add regression tests for each addressed case, covering valid configurations and invalid configurations as appropriate. Compare supported outputs against a PyTorch reference.

Existing relevant sharded and causal softmax tests continue to pass, and existing supported configurations retain their behavior.

💡 Problem to Solve

The sharded softmax factory, mask readers, and validation do not consistently enforce or honor the assumptions used to walk masks:

A row-major mask with is_causal_mask=True can select a reader that does not follow the causal compute’s per-row mask consumption, causing a hang.

Causal interleaved readers can wrap mask rows using the input width rather than the mask height, leading to incorrect/out-of-bounds reads for non-square masks.

When a shard spans a batch boundary, integer division in the per-batch core calculation can make mask addressing advance to the next batch too early.

Validation checks mask layout and padded shape but does not ensure that a sharded mask’s shard specification matches the input’s expected distribution.

title: [Bounty proposal] Fix ttnn.grid_sample memory_config overrides, sharded/interleaved factories, and padding OOB reads
author: tomisu76
body:
### Summary

`ttnn.grid_sample` (`ttnn/cpp/ttnn/operations/pool/grid_sample/`) currently contains three related memory-configuration and bounds-checking defects across `GridSampleOperation::compute_output_specs`, `GridSampleBilinearProgramFactory`, `GridSampleNearestProgramFactory`, and the dataflow kernels:

1. **Caller-provided `memory_config` is silently ignored when `grid` is `HEIGHT_SHARDED` (`grid_sample_device_operation.cpp:198-270, 331`)**:
   - In `ttnn::prim::grid_sample` (`grid_sample_device_operation.cpp:331`), `.output_mem_config` defaults to `memory_config.value_or(grid.memory_config())`, which carries `grid.shard_spec()` even when `memory_config` is omitted.
   - To avoid using `grid`'s coordinate shard width (`2*K` or `6*K`) as the output shard width (`C` or `C*K`), `compute_output_specs` guards both the `INTERLEAVED` bilinear branch (`line 200`) and the explicit `shard_spec().has_value()` branch (`line 206`) with `!grid_tensor.memory_config().is_sharded()`.
   - Consequently, whenever `grid_tensor` is `HEIGHT_SHARDED`:
     - Passing `memory_config=ttnn.DRAM_MEMORY_CONFIG` or `ttnn.L1_MEMORY_CONFIG` (`INTERLEAVED`) in `bilinear` mode is **silently ignored** and replaced with a `HEIGHT_SHARDED` L1 output on `grid_tensor`'s core grid.
     - Passing a custom `HEIGHT_SHARDED` `memory_config` with a different `ShardSpec` (core grid, orientation, or shard height) in either `nearest` or `bilinear` mode is **silently ignored** and replaced with `grid_tensor`'s `ShardSpec`.

2. **Program factories conflate `grid_tensor.is_sharded()` with `output_tensor.is_sharded()` (`grid_sample_bilinear_program_factory.cpp:33, 60-82, 202-216, 367-452` and `grid_sample_nearest_program_factory.cpp:29, 51-74`)**:
   - Both `GridSampleBilinearProgramFactory::create_descriptor` and `GridSampleNearestProgramFactory::create_descriptor` set `is_sharded = grid_tensor.is_sharded()` and assume `grid_tensor` and `output_tensor` always have identical sharding state, core grids, orientations, and corresponding shard heights.
   - In `GridSampleBilinearProgramFactory`:
     - When `grid_tensor` is `INTERLEAVED` and `output_tensor` is `HEIGHT_SHARDED`, `is_sharded` is `false`, so `output_cb` is left unbacked (`nullptr`), work is partitioned across the full device compute grid instead of `output_tensor.shard_spec().grid`, and `writer_grid_sample_interleaved.cpp` attempts interleaved page writes into a sharded L1 output buffer.
     - When `grid_tensor` is `HEIGHT_SHARDED` and `output_tensor` is `INTERLEAVED`, `output_tensor.shard_spec().value()` throws `std::bad_optional_access`.
   - In both factories, when `grid_tensor` and `output_tensor` are both `HEIGHT_SHARDED` with different `ShardSpec`s, aliasing `grid_cb` directly to `grid_tensor.buffer()` reads mismatched local L1 shards instead of reading `grid_tensor` pages via `TensorAccessor`.

3. **Out-of-bounds NoC reads on trailing shard padding sticks (`writer_grid_sample_nearest_sharded.cpp:227-235` and `reader_grid_sample_interleaved_start_id.cpp:29, 72-97`)**:
   - In `writer_grid_sample_nearest_sharded.cpp:227-235`, `if constexpr (!is_sharded) { noc.async_read(grid_tensor_accessor, ..., {.page_id = grid_stick_idx + start_page_id}, {}); }` executes **before** `if (curr_batch < batch_size)`. When an output shard has trailing padding sticks (`curr_batch >= batch_size`), it issues out-of-bounds NoC reads past the end of `grid_tensor` before discarding the read data in the `else` branch.
   - In `reader_grid_sample_interleaved_start_id.cpp:29, 72-97`, `ct_arg[5]` (`input_batch`) is passed by `GridSampleBilinearProgramFactory` (`:228`) but ignored by the kernel. When `output_tensor` is `HEIGHT_SHARDED` with uneven shards or surplus cores (`curr_batch >= input_batch`), `spatial_pos` reads past the end of `grid_tensor` instead of pushing zero-weight placeholder pages to `scalar_dfb` and `input_dfb`.

---

### Proposed Fix

1. **`grid_sample_device_operation.cpp`**:
   - In `ttnn::prim::grid_sample`, when `memory_config` is omitted, default `.output_mem_config` to `MemoryConfig(grid.memory_config().memory_layout(), grid.memory_config().buffer_type())` (with `shard_spec = std::nullopt`) so `output_mem_config.shard_spec().has_value()` is `true` if and only if the caller explicitly supplied a `ShardSpec`.
   - In `GridSampleOperation::compute_output_specs`, respect `INTERLEAVED` `output_mem_config` in `bilinear` mode and explicit `output_mem_config.shard_spec()` in both `nearest` and `bilinear` modes regardless of whether `grid_tensor` is sharded.
   - In `GridSampleOperation::validate_on_program_cache_miss`, validate explicit output `ShardSpec` buffer type (`L1`), height divisibility (`output_sticks_per_grid_stick`), and width (`C_padded`).
2. **`grid_sample_nearest_program_factory.cpp` & `grid_sample_bilinear_program_factory.cpp`**:
   - Gate the zero-copy local L1 `grid_cb` fast path (`is_sharded`) on `grid_tensor` and `output_tensor` both being sharded with matching `grid`, `orientation`, and corresponding `shape[0]`.
   - In `GridSampleBilinearProgramFactory`, separate `is_output_sharded = output_tensor.is_sharded()` from `is_sharded` so `HEIGHT_SHARDED <-> INTERLEAVED` and distinct `HEIGHT_SHARDED` `ShardSpec`s partition work and configure `output_cb` / `has_writer` / `enable_split_reader` accurately.
3. **`writer_grid_sample_nearest_sharded.cpp` & `reader_grid_sample_interleaved_start_id.cpp`**:
   - Move the `!is_sharded` `grid_tensor_accessor` NoC read inside `if (curr_batch < batch_size)` in `writer_grid_sample_nearest_sharded.cpp`.
   - Read `input_batch = get_compile_time_arg_val(5)` in `reader_grid_sample_interleaved_start_id.cpp` and guard `grid_tensor_accessor` reads with `if (curr_batch < input_batch)`, pushing zero-weight placeholder pages when `curr_batch >= input_batch`.
4. **`tests/ttnn/unit_tests/operations/pool/test_grid_sample.py`**:
   - Add unit test coverage for `HEIGHT_SHARDED` grid -> `INTERLEAVED` (`DRAM`/`L1`) output in `bilinear` mode, `INTERLEAVED` grid -> custom `HEIGHT_SHARDED` output with trailing shard padding sticks, and `HEIGHT_SHARDED` grid -> distinct `HEIGHT_SHARDED` `ShardSpec` output in both `nearest` and `bilinear` modes.

title: [Bounty proposal] Fix ttnn.rotate crashes, device hangs, and CB misbinding across sharded/interleaved memory_config transitions
author: tomisu76
body:
### Summary

`ttnn.rotate` accepts an explicit output `memory_config` parameter (`ttnn.rotate(input_tensor, angle, ..., memory_config=...)`), and `RotateDeviceOperation::compute_output_specs` supports creating either sharded or interleaved output tensors independently of the input tensor's memory configuration.

However, both `NearestProgramFactory` and `BilinearProgramFactory` conflate input sharding with output sharding (`any_sharded`), resulting in multiple deterministic host crashes (`std::bad_optional_access`, `TT_FATAL`), L1 circular buffer aliasing bugs, and a device hang when `input_tensor.memory_config()` and the requested output `memory_config` differ or when an output shard grid has surplus cores.

---

### Root Cause Analysis (Verified on `main` @ `0de8c7f3aade6170fc456b904dbf72e3f776b6aa`)

#### 1. `NearestProgramFactory::create_descriptor` crashes with `std::bad_optional_access` and misbinds `output_cb` when input is `HEIGHT_SHARDED` and output is `INTERLEAVED` (`DRAM` or `L1`)
- In [`ttnn/cpp/ttnn/operations/pool/rotate/device/rotate_nearest_program_factory.cpp#L94-L100`](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/blob/0de8c7f3aade6170fc456b904dbf72e3f776b6aa/ttnn/cpp/ttnn/operations/pool/rotate/device/rotate_nearest_program_factory.cpp#L94-L100):
  ```cpp
  if (is_sharded && !is_nd_sharded) {
      const auto input_shard_spec = input_tensor.shard_spec().value();
      all_cores = input_shard_spec.grid;
      num_cores = input_shard_spec.num_cores();
      input_nsticks_per_core = input_shard_spec.shape[0];
      output_nsticks_per_core = output_tensor.shard_spec().value().shape[0];
  ```
  `is_sharded` only checks `input_tensor.is_sharded()`. When `output_tensor` is `DRAM_MEMORY_CONFIG` or `L1_MEMORY_CONFIG` (interleaved), `output_tensor.shard_spec()` is `std::nullopt`, throwing `std::bad_optional_access`.
- In [`rotate_nearest_program_factory.cpp#L134-L135`](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/blob/0de8c7f3aade6170fc456b904dbf72e3f776b6aa/ttnn/cpp/ttnn/operations/pool/rotate/device/rotate_nearest_program_factory.cpp#L134-L135):
  `aligned_output_stick_nbytes` checks `any_sharded` (which is derived solely from `input_tensor`) instead of checking whether `output_tensor` is sharded, using an unaligned stick size when writing from a sharded input to a DRAM-interleaved output (or vice versa).
- In [`rotate_nearest_program_factory.cpp#L184-L196`](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/blob/0de8c7f3aade6170fc456b904dbf72e3f776b6aa/ttnn/cpp/ttnn/operations/pool/rotate/device/rotate_nearest_program_factory.cpp#L184-L196):
  `output_cb` is only a burst staging FIFO between `reader_rotate_nearest_interleaved.cpp` and `writer_rotate_nearest_interleaved.cpp` (which always writes every output stick via `TensorAccessor` `output_tensor_accessor`). Binding `.buffer = any_sharded ? output_tensor.buffer() : nullptr` fails with `TT_FATAL: Only L1 buffers can have an associated circular buffer!` when `output_tensor` is in DRAM, corrupts L1 when `output_tensor` is L1 interleaved, and causes race conditions when `input_tensor` and `output_tensor` have different `HEIGHT_SHARDED` shard specs.

#### 2. `BilinearProgramFactory::create_descriptor` fails when input is `HEIGHT_SHARDED` and output is `INTERLEAVED` (or uses a different `HEIGHT_SHARDED` spec)
- In [`ttnn/cpp/ttnn/operations/pool/rotate/device/rotate_bilinear_program_factory.cpp#L136`](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/blob/0de8c7f3aade6170fc456b904dbf72e3f776b6aa/ttnn/cpp/ttnn/operations/pool/rotate/device/rotate_bilinear_program_factory.cpp#L136), `const bool any_sharded = is_input_sharded || is_output_sharded;` is used to configure `output_cb` ([L201-L215](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/blob/0de8c7f3aade6170fc456b904dbf72e3f776b6aa/ttnn/cpp/ttnn/operations/pool/rotate/device/rotate_bilinear_program_factory.cpp#L201-L215)) and to skip creating `writer_desc` ([L318](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/blob/0de8c7f3aade6170fc456b904dbf72e3f776b6aa/ttnn/cpp/ttnn/operations/pool/rotate/device/rotate_bilinear_program_factory.cpp#L318), [L377](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/blob/0de8c7f3aade6170fc456b904dbf72e3f776b6aa/ttnn/cpp/ttnn/operations/pool/rotate/device/rotate_bilinear_program_factory.cpp#L377)).
- When `is_input_sharded && !is_output_sharded`:
  - `output_cb` is bound to `output_tensor.buffer()` (throwing `TT_FATAL: Only L1 buffers can have an associated circular buffer!` for DRAM output, or aliasing the interleaved L1 buffer across cores), and `writer_grid_sample_interleaved.cpp` is never launched to drain `output_cb`.
- Furthermore, `reader_rotate_bilinear_interleaved.cpp` reads from `input_tensor` exclusively via `TensorAccessor` (`input_tensor_accessor`) into an unbacked local `input_cb`. Only `output_cb` is backed by a tensor buffer when `is_output_sharded` is true. Partitioning cores by `output_shard_spec` when `is_output_sharded` is true and by `split_work_to_cores` when `is_output_sharded` is false allows `BilinearProgramFactory` to handle any combination of `HEIGHT_SHARDED` and `INTERLEAVED` inputs/outputs (including uneven shards and distinct input/output shard specs).

#### 3. `BilinearProgramFactory::create_descriptor` hangs the device when `output_shard_spec.grid` has more cores than active stick shards
- In [`rotate_bilinear_program_factory.cpp#L114-L123`](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/blob/0de8c7f3aade6170fc456b904dbf72e3f776b6aa/ttnn/cpp/ttnn/operations/pool/rotate/device/rotate_bilinear_program_factory.cpp#L114-L123):
  ```cpp
  } else if (is_output_sharded) {
      const auto output_shard_spec = output_tensor.shard_spec().value();
      output_nsticks_per_core = output_shard_spec.shape[0];
      num_cores = (total_output_sticks + output_nsticks_per_core - 1) / output_nsticks_per_core;
      all_cores = output_shard_spec.grid;
  ```
  Both `reader_desc` and `compute_desc_group_1` (`total_interpolations = output_nsticks_per_core`) are launched on `all_cores` (`output_shard_spec.grid`), but runtime arguments are only populated for `num_cores`. If `output_shard_spec.grid.num_cores() > num_cores` (e.g. 100 sticks with `shard_height = 36` on a 4-core grid), the remaining core(s) receive default `num_sticks = 0` in the reader while `compute_pool_2d` blocks indefinitely waiting for `output_nsticks_per_core` pages. Setting `num_cores = output_shard_spec.num_cores()` matches the `is_input_sharded` path, allowing `reader_rotate_bilinear_interleaved.cpp` to push fill pages for `curr_batch >= input_batch`.

#### 4. Missing output `memory_config` validation in `RotateDeviceOperation::validate_inputs`
- [`rotate_device_operation.cpp#L60-L66`](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/blob/0de8c7f3aade6170fc456b904dbf72e3f776b6aa/ttnn/cpp/ttnn/operations/pool/rotate/device/rotate_device_operation.cpp#L60-L66) validates `input.memory_config()`, but never validates `operation_attributes.memory_config` (allowing `WIDTH_SHARDED`/`BLOCK_SHARDED` output configs, mismatched shard widths, or `ND_SHARDED` configs in bilinear mode to reach the program factories and crash).

---

### Minimal Reproducer

```python
import torch
import ttnn

def test_repro(device):
    torch_input = torch.randn((1, 8, 8, 64), dtype=torch.bfloat16)
    shard_spec = ttnn.ShardSpec(
        ttnn.CoreRangeSet({ttnn.CoreRange(ttnn.CoreCoord(0, 0), ttnn.CoreCoord(1, 0))}),
        (32, 64),
        ttnn.ShardOrientation.ROW_MAJOR,
    )
    sharded_cfg = ttnn.MemoryConfig(ttnn.TensorMemoryLayout.HEIGHT_SHARDED, ttnn.BufferType.L1, shard_spec)

    ttnn_in_sharded = ttnn.from_torch(
        torch_input, layout=ttnn.ROW_MAJOR_LAYOUT, device=device, memory_config=sharded_cfg
    )

    # 1. Nearest: HEIGHT_SHARDED input -> DRAM_MEMORY_CONFIG output
    # Crashes on main with: std::bad_optional_access at rotate_nearest_program_factory.cpp:99
    out_nearest = ttnn.rotate(
        ttnn_in_sharded, angle=45.0, interpolation_mode="nearest", memory_config=ttnn.DRAM_MEMORY_CONFIG
    )

    # 2. Bilinear: HEIGHT_SHARDED input -> DRAM_MEMORY_CONFIG output
    # Crashes on main with: TT_FATAL: Only L1 buffers can have an associated circular buffer!
    out_bilinear = ttnn.rotate(
        ttnn_in_sharded, angle=45.0, interpolation_mode="bilinear", memory_config=ttnn.DRAM_MEMORY_CONFIG
    )
```

---

### Proposed Fix

1. **`rotate_device_operation.cpp`**: Validate `operation_attributes.memory_config` (require `HEIGHT_SHARDED` in `L1` and matching channel shard width when sharded, and require legacy `ShardSpec` in `bilinear` mode).
2. **`rotate_nearest_program_factory.cpp`**: Decouple input sharding from output sharding when computing `aligned_output_stick_nbytes`, remove the unconditional `output_tensor.shard_spec().value()` dereference, and keep `output_cb` as a local double-buffered burst FIFO (`num_cb_pages * NEAREST_BUFFERING_FACTOR`, `.buffer = nullptr`).
3. **`rotate_bilinear_program_factory.cpp`**: Drive output CB backing and core partitioning by `is_output_sharded` (using `num_cores = output_shard_spec.num_cores()` to prevent hangs on surplus grid cores, and using `split_work_to_cores` + `writer_grid_sample_interleaved.cpp` whenever `!is_output_sharded`).
4. **`test_rotate.py`**: Add unit tests covering `HEIGHT_SHARDED <-> INTERLEAVED` (`DRAM`/`L1`), `HEIGHT_SHARDED -> HEIGHT_SHARDED` with distinct shard grids/heights, uneven sharding with surplus grid cores, and invalid output `memory_config` rejection.

title: [Bounty proposal] Fix ttnn.upsample BLOCK_SHARDED + COL_MAJOR core-coord swap, stick_nbytes divisor, and config shard orientation (re-enables #17795 tests)
author: HindsightWise
body:
## Summary

Issue #17795 ("Re-enable COL_MAJOR test cases for `ttnn.upsample`") is now **closed**, but `tests/ttnn/unit_tests/operations/pool/test_upsample.py` still skips all `BLOCK_SHARDED` + `ShardOrientation.COL_MAJOR` cases (`pytest.skip("Disabled until illegal shard configs are fixed (#17795)")`).

Inspecting `UpsampleMultiCoreShardedProgramFactory` in `ttnn/cpp/ttnn/operations/pool/upsample/device/upsample_program_factory_multicore_sharded.cpp` reveals **three C++ bugs** when `input` is `BLOCK_SHARDED` with `ShardOrientation::COL_MAJOR` (plus an axis-limit order bug in `test_upsample.py:181-200` when `core_range=None`):

1. **`create_config_tensor` swaps `(x, y)` logical core coordinates on `BLOCK_SHARDED` + `COL_MAJOR`**: passes `CoreCoord(i, logical_core_to_stick_map[j].core_y)` where `i` is the channel core index on **Y** and `logical_core_to_stick_map[j].core_y` is the NHW core index on **X**.
2. **`create_program_artifacts` divides `input_stick_nbytes` and `output_stick_nbytes` by `ncores_x` instead of the channel-axis core count**: for `COL_MAJOR`, channels are partitioned along **Y** (`end_coord.y - start_coord.y + 1`), not **X** (`end_coord.x - start_coord.x + 1`).
3. **`create_program_artifacts` hardcodes `ShardOrientation::COL_MAJOR` for `config_shard_spec` on all `BLOCK_SHARDED` inputs**: `create_config_tensor` loops over channel cores in the outer loop and NHW cores in the inner loop, which produces `COL_MAJOR` core order when `shard_spec.orientation == ROW_MAJOR`, but **`ROW_MAJOR` core order** (`Y` outer, `X` inner) when `shard_spec.orientation == COL_MAJOR`.

---

## Location

File: `ttnn/cpp/ttnn/operations/pool/upsample/device/upsample_program_factory_multicore_sharded.cpp`

### Bug 1 — Swapped logical `(x, y)` coordinates in `create_config_tensor` (Lines 66–75, 120, 183–186)

At lines 66–75:
```cpp
        if (shard_spec.orientation == ShardOrientation::ROW_MAJOR) {
            ch_start_core = all_cores.ranges().begin()->start_coord.x;
            ch_end_core = all_cores.ranges().begin()->end_coord.x;
            nhw_start_core = all_cores.ranges().begin()->start_coord.y;
        } else {
            ch_start_core = all_cores.ranges().begin()->start_coord.y;
            ch_end_core = all_cores.ranges().begin()->end_coord.y;
            nhw_start_core = all_cores.ranges().begin()->start_coord.x;
        }
```
And at line 120:
```cpp
        logical_core_to_stick_map.emplace_back(0, nhw_start_core + core_idx, stick_offset);
```
When `shard_spec.orientation == ShardOrientation::COL_MAJOR`, `i` in `for (size_t i = ch_start_core; i <= ch_end_core; i++)` is the **Y** coordinate and `logical_core_to_stick_map[j].core_y` (`nhw_start_core + core_idx`) is the **X** coordinate. Yet lines 183–186 unconditionally construct `CoreCoord(i, logical_core_to_stick_map[j].core_y)`:
```cpp
                core_coords = device.worker_core_from_logical_core(
                    is_height_sharded
                        ? CoreCoord(logical_core_to_stick_map[j].core_x, logical_core_to_stick_map[j].core_y)
                        : CoreCoord(i, logical_core_to_stick_map[j].core_y));
```
On non-square or asymmetrically offset grids (e.g. `(0, 0)-(1, 3)`), `CoreCoord(y, x)` indexes outside the shard grid (or throws `TT_FATAL` in `worker_core_from_logical_core` when `end_coord.y >= compute_grid.x`). On square grids where an input row straddles two NHW cores, cross-core NoC reads fetch sticks from the wrong channel shard.

### Bug 2 — Wrong channel-core divisor for `input_stick_nbytes` / `output_stick_nbytes` (Lines 311–315)

```cpp
    // extra limitation to avoid post upsample step of resharding
    if (input.memory_config().memory_layout() == TensorMemoryLayout::BLOCK_SHARDED) {
        ncores_x = all_cores.ranges().begin()->end_coord.x - all_cores.ranges().begin()->start_coord.x + 1;
        input_stick_nbytes = input_stick_nbytes / ncores_x;
        output_stick_nbytes = output_stick_nbytes / ncores_x;
    }
```
Under `BLOCK_SHARDED` + `COL_MAJOR`, NHW is sharded along X and channels are sharded along Y (matching `compute_num_cores_nhw` in `upsample_common.cpp:21-24` and `get_cores_with_work` at line 240). Dividing `input_stick_nbytes` and `output_stick_nbytes` by `ncores_x` instead of the channel-axis extent (`end_coord.y - start_coord.y + 1` for `COL_MAJOR`) miscomputes `in_dfb`, `out_dfb`, and the kernel `stick_nbytes` compile-time arg on any non-square grid.

### Bug 3 — Unconditional `ShardOrientation::COL_MAJOR` for `config_shard_spec` (Lines 332–336)

```cpp
    const auto config_tensor_shard_orientation =
        input.memory_config().memory_layout() == TensorMemoryLayout::BLOCK_SHARDED ? ShardOrientation::COL_MAJOR
                                                                                   : shard_spec.orientation;
    // Use cores_with_work for config tensor sharding - only cores that have actual work need config data
    const ShardSpec config_shard_spec(cores_with_work, shard_shape, config_tensor_shard_orientation);
```
In `create_config_tensor`, the outer loop iterates over channel cores (`ch_start_core .. ch_end_core`) and the inner loop iterates over NHW cores (`nhw_start_core ..`).
- When `shard_spec.orientation == ROW_MAJOR` (channels on X, NHW on Y), outer=X and inner=Y emits per-core rows in `COL_MAJOR` core order.
- When `shard_spec.orientation == COL_MAJOR` (channels on Y, NHW on X), outer=Y and inner=X emits per-core rows in **`ROW_MAJOR` core order**.
Hardcoding `ShardOrientation::COL_MAJOR` distributes config rows in `COL_MAJOR` order while they were generated in `ROW_MAJOR` order.

---

## Proposed Fix

1. **`ttnn/cpp/ttnn/operations/pool/upsample/device/upsample_program_factory_multicore_sharded.cpp`**:
   - **Lines 183–186**: Construct `CoreCoord(i, logical_core_to_stick_map[j].core_y)` when `shard_spec.orientation == ShardOrientation::ROW_MAJOR` and `CoreCoord(logical_core_to_stick_map[j].core_y, i)` when `ShardOrientation::COL_MAJOR`.
   - **Lines 311–315**: Compute `ncores_ch` along X for `ROW_MAJOR` and along Y for `COL_MAJOR`, and divide `input_stick_nbytes` / `output_stick_nbytes` by `ncores_ch`.
   - **Lines 332–336**: For `BLOCK_SHARDED`, set `config_tensor_shard_orientation` to `ShardOrientation::COL_MAJOR` when `shard_spec.orientation == ShardOrientation::ROW_MAJOR`, and `ShardOrientation::ROW_MAJOR` when `shard_spec.orientation == ShardOrientation::COL_MAJOR`.
2. **`tests/ttnn/unit_tests/operations/pool/test_upsample.py`**:
   - In `upsample_multicore_common` (`core_range is None`), bound `max_nshards_h` / `max_nshards_w` by the orientation-appropriate grid axes and pass `(ncores[1], ncores[0])` to `get_shard_grid_from_num_cores` when `BLOCK` + `COL_MAJOR` (matching the `core_range != None` branch at lines 162–165).
   - Remove the two stale `#17795` `pytest.skip` guards in `test_upsample_multicore` and `test_upsample_multicore_corerange`.

---

## Reproduction & Verification

```python
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import ttnn

device = ttnn.open_device(device_id=0, l1_small_size=24576)
torch.manual_seed(0)

# Non-square 2x4 grid (0,0)-(1,3), BLOCK_SHARDED + COL_MAJOR
# 2 NHW cores along X (8 sticks/core), 4 channel cores along Y (32 ch/core)
x_nchw = torch.randn((1, 128, 4, 4), dtype=torch.bfloat16)
x_nhwc = x_nchw.permute(0, 2, 3, 1).contiguous()
golden = nn.functional.interpolate(x_nchw.float(), scale_factor=(2, 2), mode="nearest").bfloat16().permute(0, 2, 3, 1)

grid = ttnn.CoreRangeSet({ttnn.CoreRange(ttnn.CoreCoord(0, 0), ttnn.CoreCoord(1, 3))})
shard_spec = ttnn.ShardSpec(grid, (8, 32), ttnn.ShardOrientation.COL_MAJOR)
mem_cfg = ttnn.MemoryConfig(ttnn.TensorMemoryLayout.BLOCK_SHARDED, ttnn.BufferType.L1, shard_spec)

tt_in = ttnn.from_torch(x_nhwc, dtype=ttnn.bfloat16, layout=ttnn.ROW_MAJOR_LAYOUT, device=device, memory_config=mem_cfg)
tt_out = ttnn.upsample(tt_in, (2, 2), mode="nearest")
out = ttnn.to_torch(tt_out)
assert torch.equal(out, golden)
ttnn.close_device(device)
```

---

## Bounty Request

Given that:
1. Issue #17795 is closed, but all `BLOCK_SHARDED` + `COL_MAJOR` tests in `test_upsample.py` remain skipped due to these three C++ bugs in `UpsampleMultiCoreShardedProgramFactory`
2. The bugs cause silent data corruption on square grids (1,792 / 3,072 mismatched elements on `H=3, W=4, C=64`) and out-of-grid core lookups + 2x stick-size miscalculation on rectangular grids
3. The fix cleanly resolves all three C++ defects and re-enables the full `COL_MAJOR` test matrix in `test_upsample.py`

I propose a **$750 bounty** for this fix (similar to #64575 and #64647). I have the complete patch and regression tests ready to submit if assigned.

— submitted with Antigravity on the contributor's behalf

title: CPU mining capped at 64 threads on Windows machines with 64+ logical cores
author: brianp
body:
## Bounty: Fix CPU mining 64-thread cap on Windows (64+ logical cores)

**Tier:** M — 60,000 XTM

### Description

CPU mining tops out at 64 threads on Windows machines that have more than 64 logical cores. A user with 128 threads reported that only 64 were ever used, no matter what thread count they selected. The goal of this bounty is simple to state and hard to prove: **make Tari Universe actually use more than 64 threads on a Windows machine that has more than 64 logical cores.**

Windows splits machines with more than 64 logical processors into "processor groups" of at most 64 each, and a process that isn't group-aware only gets scheduled onto one group. On top of that, Rust's `std::thread::available_parallelism()` (which we use to count cores) undercounts past 64 on Windows for the same reason. The correct fix must count cores across all processor groups **and** ensure the miner threads actually run across them — however that is best achieved.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] On a Windows machine with **more than 64 logical cores**, CPU mining uses **more than 64 threads** — up to the count the user selects, bounded by the machine's real logical core count
- [ ] Core count is determined accurately across all processor groups (not capped at 64 the way `available_parallelism()` is)
- [ ] No regression on machines with ≤64 cores, and no regression on macOS or Linux
- [ ] **The PR includes proof of a working result on real hardware:**
  - [ ] A screenshot proving the test machine's spec (Task Manager → Performance, or CPU-Z) showing **more than 64 logical cores**
  - [ ] Screenshots and/or xmrig log excerpts showing **more than 64 threads in active use** after the fix, on that machine

### Development Requirements

This bounty **cannot be developed or verified blind.** You must have access to a Windows machine with more than 64 logical cores to work on it. A fix that "looks correct" but is not demonstrated to work on qualifying hardware will **not** be accepted — the hardware proof above is mandatory, not optional. A VM/emulated core count that does not reproduce real processor-group behavior does not qualify. If you do not have such a machine, this is not the right bounty for you.

### Context

- Relevant code:
  - `src-tauri/src/mining/cpu/manager.rs` — `determine_number_of_cores_to_use()` uses `thread::available_parallelism()`, which undercounts past 64 on Windows
  - `src-tauri/src/mining/cpu/miners/xmrig.rs` — passes the count through as `--threads={cpu_threads}`
  - xmrig is pinned to `6.25.0` in `src-tauri/binaries-versions/binaries_versions_*.json`
- **Open question (see the analysis in the comment below):** it is not yet confirmed whether xmrig 6.25.0 spreads threads across processor groups on its own. The comment below is a *lead/hypothesis*, not a confirmed ceiling — do not treat it as ruling out an app-side fix. The bounty is open to any approach that demonstrably works: an accurate all-groups core count, adjusting how xmrig is launched (e.g. affinity handling on Win11/Server 2022), or a launcher strategy. What matters is the proven result on real hardware, not the mechanism.
- Reference on the 64-core threshold and Windows processor groups: https://bitsum.com/general/the-64-core-threshold-processor-groups-and-windows/

### How It Works

1. Comment on this issue to signal intent (courtesy, not a lock)
2. Fork the repo and do the work
3. Submit a PR that references the issue with a closing keyword (e.g. `Fixes #3299`) so GitHub links your PR to the bounty automatically
4. Bounties are competitive. Multiple PRs may be submitted for the same bounty. Review comments are public, and contributors may borrow ideas from each other's work. The maintainer selects the PR that best solves the problem, considering code quality, completeness, and contributor behavior. In cases where multiple contributors made significant contributions, the maintainer may split the bounty. The maintainer's decision is final.
5. Earn XTM (processing may take up to a week; reach out to @possum on Discord with your Tari address)

### Notes

- AI-assisted development is expected and encouraged
- If you get stuck, ask in Discord

# Bounty: Reproducible Wallet Performance Test Harness

**Tier:** L — 150,000 XTM

## Description

Build a reproducible test harness that measures `minotari-cli` wallet performance across three modes: old wallet (`minotari_console_wallet` via gRPC), new wallet (`minotari-cli` library with offline signing), and payment processor (batch 1-to-many transactions via `minotari-cli`).

Implementation approach is up to you — Rust, Python, shell scripts, or any combination — as long as the results are reproducible and verifiable by a third party running the same harness against the same network.

## Deliverables

1. **Harness source code** in a new repo, buildable and runnable by anyone with access to a funded wallet on Esmeralda testnet.
2. **Run instructions** — complete, step-by-step, no implicit knowledge.
3. **Baseline result profile** — a structured report generated by running the harness, committed alongside the code, serving as proof the harness works and as a reference point for future comparisons.

## Wallet Modes

1. **Old Wallet (`minotari_console_wallet`)** — harness manages the wallet process lifecycle (spawn, wait for ready, run tests, tear down) and interacts via gRPC.
2. **New Wallet (`minotari-cli` library)** — uses the `minotari` crate directly: local UTXO selection, `sign_locked_transaction`, broadcast via HTTP RPC to a base node. No external wallet process.
3. **Payment Processor** — uses the new wallet's batch transaction capability to send 1-to-many transactions.

## Configuration Parameters

The harness MUST expose (and the result profile MUST record) the following parameters. Values below are the reference defaults for the baseline result profile.

| Parameter | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `A_fund` | 10,000 tXTM | Single funding UTXO per mode. ~71% of one Esmeralda block reward. |
| `C_min` | 3 | Confirmation depth before a UTXO is treated as spendable. |
| `volume_target` | 512 UTXOs | Target UTXO count after S1. |
| `doubling_rounds` | 6 | Take 1 → 64 UTXOs. |
| `fanout_outputs_per_tx` | 8 | Take 64 → 512 UTXOs in one round of 64 txs. |
| `concurrent_batches` | 8, 16, 32, 64, 128 | Ramp for S4. |
| `S4_T_budget` | 15 min | Stop condition per batch in S4. |
| `S5_M` | 100 | Total recipients paid in S5. |
| `S5_K` | 10 | Outputs per batch tx in S5 (→ 10 batch txs vs. 100 individual txs). |
| `fee_rate` | pinned | Explicit fee rate passed to all modes. Record the value used. |
| Wallet binary versions | pinned | Exact commit/tag of `minotari_console_wallet`, `minotari-cli`, base node. |

**Seed strategy:** fresh seed per wallet mode. Funding the next mode's seed can come from anywhere (faucet, prior mode sweep-back, miner wallet) — the funding step is not part of the measurement.

## Test Protocol

Nine scenarios run per wallet mode, in the order below. Every scan scenario starts with a wiped wallet data dir. Every scenario records: wall-clock duration, fees paid, success/failure counts with reasons, and final balance delta vs. expected.
When you need to rescan from genesis, use the api to change the seed words so that the encoded birthday reflects 0.

### B0 — Baseline Scan (empty wallet)

Floor cost of block-walk + view-key check with nothing to store.

- **Preconditions:** fresh seed, never funded. Base node synced to tip. Birthday = 0.
- **Steps:** launch scan from genesis → wait for wallet height == tip.
- **Verification:** 0 UTXOs, 0 balance, 0 outputs found.
- **Metrics:** `T_scan`, `blocks_per_sec`, `H_tip_start`, `H_tip_end`, peak RSS, peak CPU%.

### S0 — Funding Baseline

Identical starting state for all downstream scenarios.

- **Preconditions:** fresh seed, fresh wallet data dir. Base node synced.
- **Steps:** init wallet → record birthday `H_birth` → receive 1 UTXO of `A_fund` → wait for confirmation at depth ≥ `C_min`.
- **Verification:** exactly 1 spendable UTXO; balance == `A_fund`.
- **Metrics:** broadcast→mempool time; broadcast→confirmed-at-depth time; `H_birth`, tip height.

### S1 — UTXO Build-up (doubling + fan-out → 512)

Produces on-chain history for scan scenarios AND measures per-tx cost.

**Doubling phase (6 rounds):**

| Round | Txs (serial) | Inputs/tx | Outputs/tx | UTXOs after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1 | 1 | 2 | 2 |
| 2 | 2 | 1 | 2 | 4 |
| 3 | 4 | 1 | 2 | 8 |
| 4 | 8 | 1 | 2 | 16 |
| 5 | 16 | 1 | 2 | 32 |
| 6 | 32 | 1 | 2 | 64 |

**Fan-out phase (1 round):** 64 txs, each 1 input → 8 outputs → 512 UTXOs.

**Per-round procedure:**
1. Snapshot balance and UTXO set.
2. Construct + broadcast all round txs serially.
3. Wait until all round txs reach depth ≥ `C_min`.
4. Refresh wallet state (tip refresh, not full scan).
5. Verify UTXO count matches target; verify `balance_after == balance_before − Σ round_fees`.

**Failure halts the scenario** — doubling cannot continue if a round's txs don't all land.

**Metrics (per tx):** construction time, broadcast→mempool time, broadcast→confirmed time, fee paid, outcome. **Per round:** wall-clock, total fees, failures. **Scenario total:** cumulative fees, cumulative wall-clock, balance reconciliation delta.

### S2 — Scan from Genesis (checkpoint 1)

- **Preconditions:** S1 complete; wipe wallet data dir; birthday = 0.
- **Steps:** launch scan from genesis → wait for height == tip.
- **Verification:** 512 spendable UTXOs rediscovered; balance matches post-S1; all S1 txs in history.
- **Metrics:** same as B0, plus outputs-found count.
- **Delta:** `T_scan(S2) − T_scan(B0)` ≈ cost of discovering/storing 512 UTXOs and their spent-input matches.

### S3 — Scan from Birthday (checkpoint 1)

Identical to S2 except **birthday = `H_birth`**. `blocks_scanned = H_tip_end − H_birth`.

### S4 — Concurrent Construction

Measures what each wallet mode does under concurrent load. Locking, serialization, selection contention, and stalls are the signal — NOT failures to engineer around.

- **Preconditions:** S1 complete.
- **Steps:** for each `N_concurrent` ∈ {8, 16, 32, 64, 128}:
  1. Pick `N_concurrent` distinct recipient addresses (self-sends OK).
  2. Fire all construction+broadcast calls in parallel (harness-level threads/async).
  3. Record per-tx: submit time, construction-complete time, broadcast outcome, confirmation time, error string.
  4. Wait for all terminal states OR `T_budget` elapsed (then record partial results and continue).
- **No retry. No backoff. No UTXO pre-partitioning.**
- **Metrics:** per-tx durations; batch wall-clock; success rate; max observed serialization gap between consecutive construction-complete events (exposes internal serialization); any double-selection rejections.

### S5 — Payment Processor Throughput

Headline comparison: batch 1-to-N vs. individual 1-to-1 sends paying the **same `M` recipients**.

- **Preconditions:** S4 complete. Record and disclose current UTXO count / balance (post-S4 state; do not normalize).
- **Recipient set:** fixed list of `M = 100` addresses, used by both arms.

**Arm A — Batch:**
- Submit `M/K = 10` batch txs (1 input → `K = 10` outputs), back-to-back.
- Wait for all confirmed at depth ≥ `C_min`.
- Record `T_batch`.

**Arm B — Individual:**
- Submit `M = 100` single-output txs, back-to-back.
- Wait for all confirmed at depth ≥ `C_min`.
- Record `T_individual`.

**Metrics:**
- `T_batch`, `T_individual`
- **Throughput multiplier = `T_individual / T_batch`** (headline)
- Total fees per arm; fee-per-recipient per arm
- Blocks consumed per arm
- Per-tx success/failure counts

**Runs per mode:** batch arm for payment processor; individual arm for new wallet and old wallet (for context).

### S6 — Scan from Genesis (checkpoint 2)

Same shape as S2 but after S5. Expected history ≈ 127 txs (S1) + S4 txs + 110 txs (S5) ≈ 250+ txs, several hundred UTXOs to rediscover.

**Delta signals:** `T_scan(S6) − T_scan(S2)` = cost of scanning S4+S5 history. `T_scan(S6) / T_scan(B0)` = scan slowdown factor vs. empty baseline.

### S7 — Scan from Birthday (checkpoint 2)

Same shape as S3 but after S5.

## Cross-cutting Metrics

Captured in every scenario:
- **Fees paid** — per tx, per round, per scenario total.
- **Error rate** — success / rejection / stall / timeout, with error strings.
- **Balance reconciliation** — `expected_balance − observed_balance` after every scenario. Flag any non-zero delta.
- **Chain tip heights** — at scenario start and end (for drift disclosure across modes).

## Result Profile (output format)

Structured output (JSON preferred, CSV acceptable), committed alongside the harness code as proof-of-run and reference baseline.

**Must include:**
- Hardware / environment disclosure: CPU model, RAM, disk type, OS, network path to base node (local vs. remote).
- Pinned versions: `minotari_console_wallet`, `minotari-cli`, base node — commit hash or release tag.
- All configuration parameter values used for the run.
- Per-scenario, per-mode block of metrics as described above.
- Computed deltas (e.g., `T_scan(S2) − T_scan(B0)`, S5 throughput multiplier).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Harness runs against Esmeralda testnet with no manual intervention beyond initial wallet funding.
- All three modes implemented; all nine scenarios (B0, S0–S7) produce results per mode.
- All configuration parameters exposed and recorded in the output.
- A third party can clone the repo, build the harness, fund the wallets, and reproduce the test — instructions are clear and complete.
- A baseline result profile is committed alongside the harness code.
- Results are output in a structured format suitable for automated comparison.
- **Harness does not hide wallet pain** (see principle below).

## Principle — Harness Measures, Does Not Engineer Around Wallet Pain

UTXO locking, selection contention, stalls, and failed tx construction under concurrency are **part of what the harness measures**. Do not add harness-level retries, backoff, UTXO pre-partitioning, throttling, or serialization that hides how a wallet mode actually behaves under load.

If a wallet stalls for 10 minutes on a locked store, that stall is the result. If a wallet mode cannot complete a scenario, that is a reportable result — not a reason to tune the harness until it does. Timeouts should be generous (so stalled-but-progressing wallets get credit for completing), but the observed behavior must show up in the metrics.

title: Write up the Exchange update process in the Tari Wiki
author: metalaureate
body:
When a release needs exchanges to act, we contact them. That process works, but it only exists in the heads of the people who do it. The community has asked us to write it down.

The deliverable is an article on wiki.tari.com covering how we run an exchange update:

- Who we contact at each exchange, and through which channel.
- What triggers an outreach, meaning which kinds of release we tell exchanges about and which we do not.
- How much notice we give.
- What the message says: version, what they need to do, and by when.
- Who at Tari Labs sends it and tracks who has responded.

Keep it to what we actually do today. If a step is currently improvised, write down what we have been doing rather than inventing a better version.

## Acceptance

The article is live on wiki.tari.com, and someone new could follow it to run the next exchange update without asking anyone how it works.

Submit as a PR against the repo backing the wiki, linked back to this issue. Retro bounty on merge.

title: online multiplayer lobby [bounty: 6666 XTR]
author: DreadKnight
body:
In order to have online multiplayer feature back up, we need to remove [Nakama](https://heroiclabs.com/nakama), as it was problematic and we only used it in order to match players together via its lobby feature, the rest of gameplay is actually p2p (we'll secure it via #1791).

We should even remove it as project dependency and have lobby feature implemented via Google's [Open Match](https://open-match.dev) -> [repo](https://github.com/googleforgames/open-match).
Or we could have our own implementation, not replying on something generic that's "one size fits all", there are upsides.

Could have this without a user system for the players, having auto-generated unique id's for now, later we'll go for #2032.

Open Match is serverless, so we should be able to host it via our sponsored servers provided by [Qoddi](https://qoddi.com), though Open Match uses Kubernets and [KinD](https://kind.sigs.k8s.io) is needed in order to host those on Docker -> https://github.com/googleforgames/open-match/blob/main/docs/development.md

Note that the current implementation of online multiplayer (using Nakama) hasn't been maintained and is probably broken; it was tested for a while until we bumped into a show-stopping bug that wasn't fixed #2044 since the coder couldn't figure it out and neither did others - so ideally that issue will be fixed or avoided in the process.

This is issue is the first vital step towards having online multiplayer -> https://github.com/orgs/FreezingMoon/projects/11

title: modular abilities [bounty: 70 XTR]
author: DreadKnight
body:
Unit abilities should be refactored by having a proper API, with a set of actions that can be combined.
They should have a common class that gets instantiated, standard object oriented programming style.

It should roughly contain stuff like:
- type (first ability is passive, second is a basic attack, third is a special move and forth is an ultimate)
- usability (certain conditions must be met in order to be able to use the ability, provided cost is fulfilled; an ability could be disable by a debuff; active abilities are usually only usable once per turn)
- cost (usable abilities have a usage cost, usually being a certain amount of energy points, but not exclusive or limited to that)
- upgrade (passive abilities tend to auto upgrade before a set amount of rounds, while the other require a certain number of uses before upgrading; when an ability is upgraded, certain parameters are improved)
- effect (this can be certain amounts of damage, healing, movement, buffs/debuffs)
- target (can be self, enemy units, allied units, area, hexagon, etc.)
- range (some abilities have patterns, basic attacks can usually hit in front and sideways of the first/last unit hexagon; )
- hits (some abilities can hit multiple times or even be used multiple times in the same round)
- modifiers (stats and masteries can influence the output of specific abilities)

Files to be refactored: `src/ability.js` and the stuff in `src/abilities`.
This is one of the biggest things holding back the project, as it makes it hard to code abilities for new awesome playable units.
